answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic stake burning per identity registration. Generating each node requires cryptographic stake destruction scaling superlinearly as O(N^2), imposing devastating economic friction against cluster spoofing. Much like how a gale shears leaves across a barren knoll, massive burn costs decimate coordinated swarms. Even if an attacker varies identity metadata like visual pigment markers, exponential cost curves ensure attacking remains mathematically unaffordable.
